facts.claim: Reported category context: NCA’s June 2026 report says 47% of American adults consumed specialty coffee in the past day. Among past-day specialty drinkers, 36% had coffee prepared outside the home, versus 23% among traditional coffee drinkers. These national aggregates are not local switching probabilities.

Reported choices: Dutch Bros Order Ahead is available at participating shops; Dunkin offers app ordering and rewards. A credible alternative depends on the particular route and location, not merely national brand availability.

Assumed character: This player is a composite of morning purchase occasions, not a single person controlling the market and not a recruited survey panel. It may describe different segment choices but may not report votes or measured percentages.
sources: Author-designed simulation assumption, 2026-09-12; not a company disclosure or measured customer observation.

facts.claim: Assumed commuter occasion: A weekday commuter buys before a fixed work start, has 10 minutes of discretionary travel-and-wait time, and an $8 coffee-and-light-breakfast ceiling. A 4-minute detour consumes real slack. These figures are illustrative constraints, not survey findings.
sources: Author-designed simulation assumption, 2026-09-12; not a company disclosure or measured customer observation.

facts.claim: Assumed habitual-app occasion: A repeat Starbucks buyer values a familiar customization and prepaid ordering, allows an 8-minute pickup delay when communicated before paying, and may switch temporarily after two unreliable mornings. Loyalty friction exists, but its monetary value and prevalence are unknown.
sources: Author-designed simulation assumption, 2026-09-12; not a company disclosure or measured customer observation.

facts.claim: Assumed café occasion: A customer intends to sit for 25 minutes before a meeting and has a $7 drink budget. Predictable handoff and an available place to sit matter; a cheap drive-through is not a complete substitute for this occasion.
sources: Author-designed simulation assumption, 2026-09-12; not a company disclosure or measured customer observation.

facts.claim: Assumed outside option and household economics: Some mornings the customer can prepare coffee at home using an illustrative $1 marginal ingredient cost; time, preparation equipment and taste differ. Skipping the purchase or buying later is permissible. These examples do not establish local market shares.

facts.claim: Assumed information rights: Customers see quoted pickup times, prices, offers, public store conditions and their own experience.
